text:
Aisha (Support): FYI customer (CorpX mobile app) opened an escalation — streaming responses cut out mid-stream ~10-30s into long generations. Happens ~3-4x/day. Customer says client sees socket close with no final chunk.
Tom (ClientOps): Can you paste the client's logs? Are they on iOS/Android? SDK version?
Aisha (Support): Android 12, our Android SDK 0.12.1. Here's the client-side log snippet they sent:
```
07:23:12.112 INFO SSE connect: GET /v1/streams-gen
07:23:13.401 INFO recv chunk 1 size=1024
07:23:25.851 WARN read timeout after 15s waiting for chunk
07:23:25.852 ERROR socket closed by client (code=1006)\n```
They also provided the partial payload (truncated mid-json):
```
event: message
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...long text..."}}]}\n
```
Marta (SRE): 1006 means abnormal closure (client/socket). Could be client timing out, OS suspending, or intermediate proxy dropping idle connection. Any ALB/NGINX in front?
Aisha (Support): Hosted stack: external ALB -> api-gateway -> redwood-ingress (nginx) -> inference service. Default ALB idle timeout is 60s but this is happening much earlier (15s in logs).
Nikhil (SDK): Android SDK has a default read timeout of 15s in okhttp if not overridden. If the model is generating slowly between chunks, okhttp may close. We added a keepalive option in later SDKs. Customer is on 0.12.1 which doesn't enable that by default.
Tom (ClientOps): Good catch. Customer says gaps of ~12-18s between partial chunks. So okhttp would close at 15s and client would drop. Two paths: increase read timeout on client, or make server emit keepalive comment lines or frequent small chunks to keep connection activity.
Aisha (Support): Customer asked if Redwood should send keepalives by default. Is that safe?
Marta (SRE): We already send small progress tokens for some models, but not guaranteed. Keepalives are safe, but we need to ensure they don't break parsers. Standard SSE keepalive is a colon-prefixed comment line (`: keepalive\n\n`). That is ignored by EventSource clients. For raw okhttp streaming they also keep the connection alive.
Nikhil (SDK): On SDK side we can add an opt-in keepalive shim in 0.13.x + a config flag to set client read timeout to 0 (no timeout) or large. Recommend: SDK sets a socket read timeout of 0 and also auto-reconnect with Last-Event-ID for resumable streams where possible. For non-idempotent generation we still need to re-request and stitch.
Aisha (Support): Customer wants immediate workaround. Suggested steps I gave them: 1) bump okhttp readTimeout to 60s, 2) upgrade SDK to >=0.13.0 when available, 3) if using own HTTP stack, add SSE keepalives server-side or client-side keepalive header. They asked for exact commands to repro — can we provide curl/node repro?
Tom (ClientOps): Yeah add a simple curl repro and a tcpdump suggestion. Also mention proxies/APNs and mobile carrier NAT timeouts — some carriers drop long-idle TCP after ~15s.
Marta (SRE): Stack repro (server-side): curl with -N to disable buffering:
```
# follow stream raw
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams-gen?model=redwood-strong"\n```
To simulate chunk gaps server-side: run netcat emulator or small Node script that writes events with delays. Example Node snippet: 
```
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req,res)=>{
  res.writeHead(200,{'Content-Type':'text/event-stream','Cache-Control':'no-cache'});
  res.write('event: message\n');
  res.write('data: {"text":"part1"}\n\n');
  setTimeout(()=>{
    res.write(': keepalive\n\n'); // comment keepalive
    // delay longer than client timeout
    setTimeout(()=> res.write('data: {"text":"part2"}\n\n'),17000);
  },5000);
}).listen(9999);
```
Nikhil (SDK): For Android quick patch:
```
okHttpClient.newBuilder().readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // disable
  .pingInterval(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS) // if using HTTP/2 pings
  .build();
```
But pingInterval requires HTTP/2 and may not apply to all stacks.
Aisha (Support): I forwarded that to customer. They replied back with more info: their mobile isn't consistently on cellular; sometimes wifi->cell transitions when backgrounding app. They also captured an app-level stacktrace showing okhttp raising SocketTimeoutException.
Tom (ClientOps): Sounds like two root causes: client read timeout + network change mid-stream. When wifi->cell happens the socket will drop and 1006 occurs. App should implement reconnect + resume logic where feasible. Also recommend the app hold the UI open and show partial content instead of retrying invisibly.
Marta (SRE): On infra side we should consider emitting lightweight keepalives from the API ingress layer for SSEs if response is slower than X seconds (X configurable). But we must check cost: extra bytes per connection. Also ensure ALB idle timeout not lower than keepalive interval.
Nikhil (SDK): I'll open SDK issue and PR: add "sse_keepalive_interval_ms" default 12000 and set okhttp read timeout to 0 by default for streaming methods. Will include docs on how to opt out.
Aisha (Support): Customer asked if we can do a temporary server-side change for their tenant to avoid them having to push an app update. Can we toggle ingress keepalive for a tenant?
Marta (SRE): We can add an ingress config flag per tenant that inserts `: keepalive\n\n` every 12s. Low risk. I'll open a runbook and schedule a rollout to enable for CorpX in staging first.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: staging/ingress-keepalive-toggle -> start 2026-03-16T16:15:00Z, estimated 5m.
Aisha (Support): Thanks team. I'll keep customer updated: temp server-side keepalives + SDK patch + client config recommended. Customer asked for checklist for their iOS team too — any iOS tips?
Nikhil (SDK): iOS (URLSession) has a default timeout for `task` as well; set `timeoutIntervalForRequest` to 0 for streaming, implement URLSessionStreamTask or use EventSource libs that handle reconnection. Also ensure background mode and connectivity handling around WiFi->cell transitions.
Tom (ClientOps): Also remind them to log network type and last-event-id + byte offset to help stitch after reconnect.
Aisha (Support): I'll update the ticket with repro steps, the Node/curl examples, recommended SDK patch, and SRE action to enable tenant-level keepalives. Closing loop once staging change is verified. :thumbsup:
Marta (SRE): I'll post status here after staging verification.
Nikhil (SDK): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/142 (draft).
Aisha (Support): Great, thanks everyone. I told the customer ETA ~48h for staging toggle + SDK timeline next week.
